name: Claudia A. Nasraty
headline: I Turn Moving Parts Into Forward Motion
tagline:
I build the structure, systems, and support that fast-moving teams need when their operations have not caught up with their pace.

When that gap exists, priorities blur and follow-through breaks down. I step in to bring clarity, ownership, and momentum, so leaders can focus on strategy instead of getting pulled into execution.

When challenges surface, I take ownership, steady the work, and turn things around.
summary:
The way I work today took shape even before I had the language for it. 

Early in my career, I joined the marketing communications department at a telecommunications company in Kabul, Afghanistan. It was an international, fast-moving multicultural environment and unlike anything I had worked in before. It taught me that getting work done is never just about tasks and timelines. It is about listening first, earning trust, and understanding how people actually work together. This experience set the foundation for everything that followed.

The relationships I have built throughout my career have lasted longer than the jobs themselves. People I have worked alongside, including leaders, have brought me into their next companies. They have seen my work up close and trusted my abilities and judgment. That is probably what I’m most proud of.

What energizes me as a professional is improving how things work and making systems feel smoother, clearer, and more supportive for the people using them. I pay close attention to what is missing, what feels unclear, and where things may start to break down.

To me strong operations is what makes great work possible. It is not about adding process for the sake of it, but the kind of clarity, structure, and follow-through that removes the obstacles so people can focus on the work itself. 

I care just as much about the people side of the work as the operational structure. The best environments I have been part of are the ones where people communicate openly, support each other, and make it genuinely easier to move forward together. That is what I am always working toward, whether or not it is in my job description.

I experiment with AI tools, focused on what they can actually do for the way work gets done. Not as a trend to keep up with, but as a practical question I bring to my own workflow first: does it actually make the work better, or does it just add a new layer to manage?
